title: Mosaic spaces generated by continua and by Peano continua: answers to three questions recorded by Lavallee
description:
Lavallee (1964) recorded three questions about Davison's mosaic spaces: whether a locally (m-strongly) connected m-continuum space must be a quasi-curve space; whether the converse of her theorem on open subspaces of m-continuum spaces holds; and Davison's question whether a locally arcwise connected mosaic space must be a quasi-curve space. We show that all three have negative answers. Davison's question is answered by published examples of Franklin and Smith-Thomas (1979) and of van Douwen (1981), once "path-determined" is identified with "curve space", and an example sketched by Curtis (1980) bears on the first question. We give self-contained constructions and proofs: a metric space without arcs, a completely regular space in which no metric continuum captures a certain convergent sequence, and a cone construction that answers the second question. We also prove affirmative results for first countable spaces. We claim no priority for these answers.

Lean formalization. Every theorem, lemma, proposition and corollary of the paper except the examples is formalized in Lean 4 (v4.35.0-rc2) with Mathlib, using only Lean's standard axioms, including the answers to all three questions (Q3 by the space G; Q2, Q1a and Q1b by the cone over G). The examples (Section 3 and the Appendix, van Douwen's space, Example 7.3) are not formalized. Lean Comparator accepted the 70 compared statements (run without the bubblewrap sandbox); the Lean project is at https://github.com/LucasAlves8Sp/Mosaic-spaces.

Status. Preprint; no independent expert has yet verified the proofs. Developed with extensive AI assistance (Claude Fable 5.2, ChatGPT Astra; Lean code by Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Opus 5.5); see AI_DISCLOSURE.md.
notes: Not yet independently peer reviewed. Mathematics Subject Classification 2020: Primary 54D55; Secondary 54D05, 54F15, 54G20.
